title: What If the Oceans Dropped 400 Feet?

scenes.text: What if the oceans dropped 400 feet? You could walk from Siberia to Alaska.
It's not a fantasy. At the peak of the last ice age, sea level was about 400 feet lower than today.
Continental shelves turned into coastal plains, and the shoreline sat far out from where it is now.
A land bridge joined Siberia and Alaska, and animals and people walked across it.
Southern Britain was joined to the Netherlands by a lowland called Doggerland, now under the North Sea.
Then the ice melted. Rivers had cut canyons into those plains, and the rising sea flooded them, forming today's fjords and bays. Much of human prehistory now lies underwater.

description:
What if the oceans dropped 400 feet?
It already happened: during the last ice age, sea level was about 120 metres lower, exposing land bridges and the lowland Doggerland.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Which coastline would you most want to walk out across? What should we run through next?
